summary: Documents the key features of RIP version 2 and the implementation experience so far, as the routing protocol criteria of RFC 1264 required before advancing RIP-2 on the standards track. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A report card for a routing protocol, showing it works well enough to be promoted.

questions: what is new in rip-2 compared to rip-1
subtitle: A report card for RIP-2: what is new, who has implemented it, and how it fared in real use.

tldr.problem: Routing Protocol Criteria (RFC 1264) require a report on a routing protocol's key features and implementation experience before it can advance on the standards track.
tldr.mechanism: The report lists what RIP-2 adds over RIP-1 (route tags, subnet masks, next hop addresses, authentication and multicasting), describes the MIB, and records three implementations plus five months of production use.
tldr.outcome: The report is a prerequisite to advancing RIP-2. It is Informational and obsoletes RFC 1387.

facts.label: New features
facts.value: Route tags, subnet masks, next hops, authentication, multicast

sections.title: Protocol Documents
sections.content:
As required by RFC 1264, this report documents the key features of RIP-2 and the implementation experience so far. It does not specify a standard.

The pieces of RIP-2 are defined elsewhere: the applicability statement in RFC 1722, the protocol description in RFC 1723, and the MIB in RFC 1724. The memo says it obsoletes RFC 1388, which updated the Routing Information Protocol of RFC 1058, and RFC 1389 for the MIB.
sections.eli5: This is a short report that points to the main rulebooks for a routing system and says why the report was needed.

sections.title: Key Features
sections.content:
RIP-2 shares the same basic algorithms as RIP-1 but adds external route tags, subnet masks, next hop addresses and authentication, and allows multicasting. The significant change from RFC 1388 is the removal of the domain field, which was left reserved for future expansion because there was no clear agreement on how to use it.

The route tag may carry information acquired from an EGP, such as an AS number, but its contents are beyond the protocol's scope. Subnet masks allow variable subnet masks and are needed for classless addressing as the CIDR work proposes. A next hop address lets a router tell others that a better next hop than itself exists, for example when another IGP runs on the same network.

Authentication uses the same extensible mechanism as OSPF, though only a plain-text password is defined so far. RIP-2 packets may be multicast instead of broadcast, which reduces the load on hosts that do not run routing protocols and avoids RIP-1 routers misreading routes whose subnet mask they cannot apply.
sections.eli5: The new version adds name tags for routes, a way to say how big each neighborhood is, shortcut hints, a secret password, and quieter announcements.

sections.title: The RIP-2 MIB
sections.content: The MIB allows monitoring and control of RIP's operation inside the router. It has global and per-interface counters and controls, plus per-peer counters that show the status of RIP-2 neighbors. It was changed to deprecate the domain, which was removed from the protocol, and converted to version 2 format.
sections.eli5: It is a dashboard with counters that lets an operator see how the router and its neighbors are doing.

sections.title: Implementations and Experience
sections.content:
The memo names three complete implementations: GATED, written by Jeffrey Honig at Cornell University; Xylogics's Annex Communication server; and one for NOS, written by Jeff White. The author tested GATED against the Xylogics implementation, found no incompatibilities, and verified the protection offered by authentication.

Xylogics had run RIP-2 on its production systems for five months on a topology with seven subnets in a class B address. The only problem was that some routers discard Version 2 packets rather than ignoring the fields not defined for Version 1, contrary to RFC 1058. The security considerations simply point back to the authentication and implementation sections.
sections.eli5: Three teams built it, they tried it with each other, and it worked, except a few older routers threw away the new messages instead of ignoring the new parts.
